scope: corrected new source packet and cheap tests only
first_failure_summary: prepare.py passes a string operand to bytes.count after it has begun creating the attempt
the generated-C hook assertion expects two calls although the generated C has one call and inject.h separately has one definition
the report-shaped missing/partial oracle fixture omits post_exec_backing_observed=false and rejects itself
archive_limitation: The archive retains candidate source but no raw unittest output; the exact failure summary is worker-reported.

additional_findings: The oracle incorrectly requires stdin.verified.bin for stdin-devnull although the production report uses a null input-artifact slot.
The oracle trusts report counters without binding actual retained files, witnesses, prefix bytes, DEVNULL output, outer wait, artifact hashes, identities or event/deadline ordering.
Patch, header and packet identities are recorded after use rather than checked against reviewed pins, and the copied patch is neither applied nor compared with the generated diff.
Build, run and root ownership programs remain execution-disabled placeholders and omit selector-0 control.
The focused tests do not cover the required adverse negative matrix.
accepted_source_intent_only: The injected header now follows required collector declarations and guards are compiler-supplied.
Missing and partial setup use checked witness writes and actual READY serialization.
Completed-wait uses real SIGTERM and observes the production interrupted latch without replacing its handler.
